sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). Engagement with HRC, CRPD, CEDAW, and CSW

1. The Charter of Demands developed by Partner CSO in partnership with Bangladesh Mahila Parishad, through consultations in four divisions and national-level validation involving WGG Young Leaders from each division, was shared with the Women’s Reform Commission formed by the Interim Government as part of the state reform initiative. The Commission members took the Charter of Demands into consideration while preparing the report.The Commission produced 433 recommendations across 15 thematic areas aimed at eliminating discrimination against women.2. Launched in August, the ‘Forum for Women’s Political Rights’ advances the position that women’s political empowerment is not only a fundamental right but also essential to the sustainability and integrity of democratic governance. The Forum leads a coordinated advocacy initiative focused on reforming political participation frameworks through sustained engagement with political parties, the Election Commission, and other key state actors to strengthen women’s representation in political decision-making spaces, including parliamentary seats and party nominations.
Engagement with HRC, CRPD, CEDAW, and CSW

One of the partners' advocacy efforts have been focussed on a scriber policy (scribe for visually impaired students) for different types of applicants in order to further disability inclusion in education and employment sector. Finally, this law was passed by the Ministry of Social Welfare for blind students in 2023. The metro rail service started in Dhaka from Uttara to different area. The service which is fully accessible for passengers with disabilities was primarily due to advocacy efforts of partner organization with the Ministry of Railway around accessibility in public transportation which includes metro services. Another Bangladesh partner organised a ‘Consultation with 10 Young Leaders for CSW68 Global Youth and Adolescent Recommendation’. In response to UN Women's call for recommendations for CSW68, a virtual consultation on December 18, 2023, engaged WGG young leaders. The aim was to document their recommendations for the priority theme of accelerating gender equality, emphasising the urgent need to address poverty, and strengthen institutions, and finance with a gender perspective.

One of the strategic partner CSO conducted an online Learning sharing Session on Disability inclusive programming with Dutch Embassy .(WDDF) organized an online learning-sharing session focusing on disability-inclusive programming in collaboration with the Dutch Embassy. WDDF, a foundation dedicated to working with and for women with disabilities, integrates disability justice into its operations. The session aimed to raise awareness of the challenges and needs of women and girls with disabilities, while encouraging active engagement in the development of inclusive practices across various organizational levels, to eliminate gender-based violence, combat discrimination, and integrate inclusive strategies into development work by bringing together experts, advocates, and stakeholders to share insights and collaborate on solutions.

Collective advocacy initiatives carried out that include the concerns of women and girls, including Women with Disabilities on SGBV

On International Day of Persons with Disabilities two strategic partners jointly conducted an advocacy initiative that focussed on the concerns and needs of women and girls with disabilities - where they critiqued the existing law and demanded inclusion of their rights and demanding implementation around the following; not using negative words to describe disability, creating accessible infrastructure in public spaces as well as for voting centers. This was particularly done with the general elections 2024 in mind, and accessibility needs of WGWDs. One advocacy initiative was undertaken to support 12 Young Leaders (YLs) in advocacy efforts across various initiatives. As part of the initiative two YLs organised the 'Uthan Boithok' advocacy initiative. Two YLs from another Foundation aimed to promote peace and inclusivity by empowering the gender diverse minority community in Chattogram. Two YLs from arranged a panel discussion on "Gender-based violence prevention and awareness" hosting District Magistrate of Kawkhali Upazila. Two YLs advocated for adolescent sex education in secondary schools to combat SGBV and four YLs from Desperately Seeking Bandarban (DSB) and Indigenous Exclusive (IE) collaborated on the 'Don’t Click my Picture.
Collective advocacy initiatives carried out that include the concerns of women and girls, including Women with Disabilities on SGBV

YLs joined collective advocacy initiatives at the national and regional level to protest against the violence against women, girls, children, WWD and marginalised communities. On 8th March, International Women’s Day was marked in Bangladesh with rallies, discussions, and advocacy actions organised by women’s rights organisations across the country under the theme “For ALL Women and Girls: Rights, Equality, Empowerment.” Events were held in Dhaka and several other districts, where a joint declaration was released highlighting urgent and relevant demands.On 5th May, the ILO in Bangladesh celebrated International Labour Day under the banner “Building Better Futures,” highlighting inclusive labour practices, workers’ rights, and equal opportunities for marginalised communities. Partner CSO was a strategic partner in this event. The initiative positioned inclusive labour practices, workers’ rights, safety and dignity, and equal opportunities for marginalised communities at the centre of public and policy-facing dialogue
